newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks drift lower amid cautious mood.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks drift lower amid cautious mood.

text.p: Madrid stocks drifted lower by the close on Tuesday after selling pressure plagued almost all sectors in lacklustre trade, dealers said.
Traders said they were focussing on January CPI due this Thursday, and said the stock market's prospects remained uncertain in the short run.
The general index fell 2.31 points, or 0.49 percent, to 473.24, while the blue-chip Ibex-35 index declined 28.09 points, or 0.52 percent, to 5,419.20.
Spain's January CPI is expected to rise 0.4 percent monthly to bring the year-on-year increase to 3.0 percent. That compares with 0.3 percent and 3.2 percent in December 1996.

Telefonica, which accounted for a good part of Tuesday's trading, slid 55 pesetas to 3,325 after state holding company SEPPa fixed the maximum price for the retail offer at just 40 pesetas below the stock's all time high at 3,385 pta.
While a high level of domestic liquidity gave support to the market, current prices were considered relatively high. The market's mood was mostly 'wait and see', dealers concluded.
"Stocks are doing fine, but the market here is lacking the strength to attack all-time record peaks again," said a dealer in Madrid.
